Note for triage: the closed base enum has no quantity/counter option, so "narrow the base" is not literally available here — the two honest fixes are (a) `steps_unavailable` citing the missing quantity base (the record is precise, but the enum cannot express its input type), or (b) keep base "noun" and record the numeral+counter restriction so the step is not blindly expanded. Everything else in the record is fine: nuance_tags [] is honest (the enum has no interval/frequency tag) and usage_contexts spoken+written match register "plain".

Variant 2 is [{base:verb, op:to-nai-stem}, {op:append, token:"ないようにする"}]. The task spec defines to-nai-stem by its own worked example (なければいけない = to-nai-stem + append "ければいけない", which only yields 書かなければいけない if to-nai-stem(書く) = 書かな). Under that definition the append token must NOT re-supply な. Executed literally: 食べる -> 食べな -> 食べな + ないようにする = 食べなないようにする; 書く -> 書かな + ないようにする = 書かなないようにする; する -> しなないようにする; くる -> こなないようにする. The corpus's own dominant convention agrees with the spec (~45 uses append tokens starting い/く/け/か vs ~12 that re-supply ない), and batch-14 gram:gp-128 encodes the identical surface form 忘れないように correctly as to-nai-stem + "いように". Fix: token "いようにする". Record's formation text ("Verbo na forma negativa curta (ない) + ようにする") is fine; only the step encoding is off by one な.

The single variant claims base "noun" with steps [none, append "おきに"], but the record's own formation restricts the host to a quantity phrase: "número + contador + おきに" (10分おきに, 1メートルおきに, 1日おきに). Negative variant is [{base:verb, op:"to-nai-stem"},{op:"append", token:"ないようにする"}]. Under the op semantics the task prompt itself defines (なければいけない = to-nai-stem + append "ければいけない", which requires 書く -> 書かな, i.e. the ない-form minus final い), to-nai-stem already supplies the な. Appending a token that starts with ない duplicates it. Executed literally: 書く -> 書かなないようにする, 食べる -> 食べなないようにする, する -> しなないようにする, くる -> 来なないようにする. The variant's own claimed example (食べないようにする) is NOT what its steps produce, which is the tell. The record's formation says "Verbo na forma negativa curta (ない) + ようにする ... 遅れないようにする", so the target string is right and only the token is wrong: it should be "いようにする". Cross-check inside this same dataset: batch-20 gram:nakereba-ikenai uses to-nai-stem + "ければいけない" -> 書かなければいけない (the prompt's canonical pair), batch-08 gram:naku-temo-ii uses to-nai-stem + "くてもいい" -> 静かじゃなくてもいい, and batch-33 gram:n3-you-ni-shimashou uses to-nai-stem + "いようにしましょう" -> 書かないようにしましょう. problems.issue: Variant 2 is [verb, to-nai-stem] + append "ないまま", doubling the な. Executed: 食べる -> 食べな -> 食べな+ないまま (example claims 食べないまま); 書く -> 書かなないまま; する -> しなないまま; くる -> こなないまま. The other four variants of this point (to-ta-form+まま, i-adj+まま, na-adj to-attributive+まま, noun+のまま) all execute correctly: 立ったまま / 書いたまま / 食べたまま / したまま / きたまま, 高いまま, 静かなまま, 学生のまま.

Variant 1 is base "noun" + append "ごろ", but the record restricts ごろ to point-in-time expressions and its nuance field names the counterexample explicitly: "Don't say 3時間ごろ" (use ぐらい for durations). Executed on the test bases, 学生 -> *学生ごろ and the record's own banned 3時間 -> *3時間ごろ; only the 7時ごろ-type example is valid. The base enum has no time-noun value and the corpus convention elsewhere (batch-06 gram:kara ex=3時から, batch-07 gram:made ex=駅まで) is to let the example carry the semantic class, so this is not a step-sequence error — but here the record itself supplies the forbidden output, so the restriction is worth carrying in note_pt rather than being dropped. Variants 2-6 all execute correctly (学生のころ, 子供だったころ / 学生だったころ, 書いたころ / 食べたころ / したころ / きたころ, 書くころ, 若いころ / 高いころ). Missing na-adjective attachment (静かだったころ) — incompleteness only, not a false rule.

nuance_tags ["humility","politeness"] misuse the enum relative to every other point that carries them. In batches 08/11/12/18/22 "humility" marks actual 謙譲語 surface forms (ございます, いたします, 〜ていただけませんか, 〜のが下手), and "politeness" marks polite-register forms. This record's register field is ["plain"] and the pattern itself is plain ことになる; the modesty the record describes is a pragmatic effect of choosing it over ことにする, not a humble/polite form. As tagged, a consumer filtering nuance_tags=humility to build a keigo lesson pulls in a plain-form N4 pattern. The tags are record-grounded (the nuance text does say "out of modesty" / "more polite") but the enum values do not mean that here.

The single variant is [na-adjective, to-adverbial] with no token pinning the lexeme 急, so nothing mechanical in the record identifies this grammar point. Executed on the test na-adjective 静か it returns 静かに — grammatical, but that is the generic な-adjective adverbial rule (already encoded as its own point), not 急に "de repente". A generator can only reach 急に if 急 is fed in from outside the steps. Every other lexical adverb in the pass took steps_unavailable for exactly this reason — いつも (batch-06), まだ (batch-07), とても (batch-10), ぜひ / ぜんぜん (batch-25) — including きっと in this same batch, so 急に is handled inconsistently with its own neighbours.

Coverage gap vs the record, not a wrong rule. The record's formation is "[Substantivo / verbo ou adjetivo na forma simples] + みたいに" and its ONLY verb example is a plain past-NEGATIVE: 知らなかったみたいに話す. The two verb variants emitted cover only to-dictionary (書く→書くみたいに) and to-ta-form (食べる→食べたみたいに), so the record's own worked example 知らなかったみたいに (and 知らないみたいに) is unreachable from the steps. Every form the steps do generate is grammatical (書くみたいに / 食べたみたいに / 学生みたいに / 静かみたいに / 高いみたいに all verified). Fix would be adding a negative branch (to-nai-stem + い / かった) rather than changing anything already present.

Asymmetric with its sibling in the same batch. The record's formation opens "Igual ao anterior" / "Same as the previous one" — the previous record (gram:nakereba-ikenai) explicitly extends to い-adjectives, な-adjectives and nouns (元気じゃなければいけない), and batch-20 correctly emits all four bases there. Here only base verb is emitted, so 高くなければならない / 静かじゃなければならない / 学生じゃなければならない are unreachable while their いけない counterparts are reachable, from records that state the same rule. The verb steps themselves execute correctly (書かなければならない, 食べなければならない, しなければならない, 来(こ)なければならない).

The two contraction variants encode replace-ending with token "て→とく" and "で→どく" — a from→to instruction inside the single token slot, not a token. The op signature is {base?, op, token?}: replace-ending has exactly one token, so a consumer takes it as the replacement ending. Executed literally on 書く: to-te-form gives 書いて, then replacing the ending with the string "て→とく" yields 買って→とく / 書いて→とく. This is the F6 instruction-as-value shape in a mechanical field, and the same run uses the plain-value convention for the same op elsewhere (token "がる", "くて"), so the two encodings cannot both be right. Fix: token "とく" / "どく", with the て vs で condition carried by splitting the variants (which this record already does correctly).

Same defect as gram:te-oku: four variants use replace-ending with tokens "て→ちゃう", "で→じゃう", "て→ちゃった", "で→じゃった". Applied literally, replace-ending substitutes the ending with the whole token string, so 食べる → 食べて → 食べて→ちゃう. The grammar underneath is correct — the voiced and unvoiced cases are properly split into separate variants, so no *読んちゃう is licensed — but the token values are unparseable by a uniform consumer. Fix: tokens "ちゃう" / "じゃう" / "ちゃった" / "じゃった".

usage_contexts is [spoken, business], but variant 3 emits 〜てごめんなさい, which the record's own formation field explicitly marks as casual ("〜てごめんなさい / 〜てごめん (casual)"). Contexts are point-level, so every variant inherits business, and a business-context selector would surface 遅れてごめんなさい alongside 遅れて申し訳ありません. The enum has casual-friends and it is unused here.

Variant 5 emits 〜てくださる, which the record's formation labels "Versão respeitosa, quando o favor vem de um superior". くださる is 尊敬語, the enum carries an exact tag (honorific), and it is not applied — nuance_tags is [request] only. The request tag itself is grounded (formation cites 〜てくれない？), so this is an omission rather than a wrong tag.

Variants 3 and 5 emit 〜ていただく and 〜ていただけますか, which the record's formation labels "Versão respeitosa". いただく is 謙譲語 and the enum carries an exact tag (humility) that is unused — nuance_tags is [request] only. Same omission class as gram:te-kureru's missing honorific.

The 7th variant encodes the record's LEXICAL exception ("Exceções: いい → よさそう") as a productive ending-replacement over the whole i-adjective class: {base:"i-adjective", op:"replace-ending", token:"いい→よさそう"} + append "な". Applied literally to any i-adjective whose surface form ends in いい, it fires. かわいい is stored in this very corpus as an N5 i-adjective (corpus/vocab/n5.json, vocab:1577200, adj_class "i_adj"), so a generator joining these steps to the vocab registry gets かわ + よさそう + な = *かわよさそうな. The general variant (い→そう) would have produced the correct かわいそうな, but a longest-match applier must prefer いい→そう... いい→よさそう, so the exception wins and licenses the wrong form. Same defect shape as the ちゃいけない case: an exception stated for one lexeme re-expressed as a rule over a whole part of speech. The variant schema has no lexical-scope field (variant keys across all 33 batches are only base/steps/example), so the fix is to drop this variant and record いい→よさそう / かっこいい・気持ちいい as a note, or restrict it to a whole-word replacement rather than an ending match.

The 8th variant mis-targets the record's other exception. The record's "ない → なさそう" is about the NEGATIVE ない (高くない → 高くなさそう, 行かない → 行かなさそう) — its own explanation contrasts stem-based 様態 そう with the full-clause 報告 そうだ, and ない there is the negative auxiliary. Encoding it as {base:"i-adjective", op:"replace-ending", token:"ない→なさそう"} does two wrong things: (a) it never reaches the case it exists for, because no verb variant carries it, so 行かない → 行かなさそう and 高くない → 高くなさそう are unreachable from these steps; (b) it instead fires on lexical -ない adjectives, where the applier must choose between it and the general い→そう rule with no data to decide — 汚い yields きたなさそうな where dictionaries give きたなそう. Not a hard ungrammaticality, so minor, but the steps do not derive from what the record actually says.

The two exception variants encode LEXEME-specific irregularities as class-wide string rules: base is "i-adjective" with replace-ending "いい→よさそう" and "ない→なさそう". The record's own formation says these are exceptions for the words いい and ない, not for the い-adjective class. Executed literally, they fire on any い-adjective whose surface merely ENDS in いい/ない: かわいい ends in いい, so the rule yields *かわよさそうな (the correct derivation is the general い→そう rule); 汚い(きたない) ends in ない, so it yields *きたなさそうな where the standard form is 汚そう. Nothing in the emitted structure tells a consumer these two variants are lexically scoped while the coexisting general variant (い→そう, base i-adjective) is productive, so a program has no way to pick correctly — a most-specific-suffix-match picks the wrong one. Note the productive variants are all correct: masu-stem+そうな/そうに gives 書きそうな・食べそうな・しそうな・きそうな, い→そう gives 高そうな/高そうに, na-adj gives 静かそうな/静かそうに, and noun is correctly not claimed. Fix: scope the two exception variants to the lexemes いい/ない (or drop them from variants and leave the irregulars to prose), because base "i-adjective" claims far more input than they accept.

problems.issue: Variant 2 is [to-nai-stem] + append "ないつもりでした", which doubles the な. Under the op semantics the prompt itself defines (なければいけない = to-nai-stem + "ければいけない", which forces to-nai-stem(書く) = 書かな, i.e. the ない-form minus its final い), and under the convention 50 of the 61 existing to-nai-stem steps in batches 01-33 follow (…+"い"→書かない, …+"かった"→書かなかった, …+"くてもいい"→書かなくてもいい, na-adj …+"くてもいい"→静かじゃなくてもいい), executing this sequence yields 書か-な + ないつもりでした. The token must be "いうちに". Same bad output for the other bases: 書く → *書かなないうちに, 食べる → *食べなないうちに, する → *しなないうちに, くる → *こなないうちに. The declared example 降らないうちに is not what the steps generate. (The other five variants of this point all execute correctly: 話しているうちに, 降っていないうちに, 熱いうちに, 静かなうちに, 学生のうちに.)

Variant 3 ([to-ta-form] + "つもりでした" → 書いたつもりでした) is grammatical Japanese but is not this record's pattern. The record's formation field lists only dictionary-form and Verbo-ない; 〜たつもりでした appears solely in the nuance field, where the record explicitly separates it as a different meaning — 'eu achava que tinha feito (mas não tinha)', uma convicção equivocada, diferente do simples plano não realizado. Filing it as an unmarked third variant of a point labelled 'eu pretendia / eu ia' means a generator asked for 'I intended to write (but didn't)' can emit 書いたつもりでした, which means 'I was under the impression I had written it'. Either drop it or keep the two meanings apart.

structure_pattern is ～という～ and the record's own formation is "[Nome/citação] + という + [substantivo]" (田中さんという人, 「猫」という映画, 日本は安全だという話) — the head noun is obligatory. Both variants stop at という, so the steps generate a bare attributive fragment and the stored examples (田中さんという, 日本は安全だという) are truncated versions of the record's own examples with the head noun cut off. A consumer generating a target form from these steps would present 田中さんという as a complete answer. Either add a final slot for the modified noun or narrow the example to something that legitimately ends in という.

nuance_tags is ["request"] only, but two of the five emitted variants are 〜ていただく and 〜ていただけますか, which the record's formation explicitly labels "Versão respeitosa" and the nuance field repeats ("em situação de respeito, prefira 〜ていただく"). The closed enum carries "humility" and "politeness", and the sibling record gram:te-itadakemasen-ka (batch-22) is tagged ["request","politeness","humility"] for the same いただく family. The batch also lists "business" in usage_contexts, which only follows from those keigo variants — so the point acknowledges the register in one mechanical field and drops it in the other. A keigo-filtered query over nuance_tags misses this point.

Same species as te-morau: nuance_tags is ["request"] only, while the variant list emits 〜てくださる, which the record's formation calls "Versão respeitosa, quando o favor vem de um superior" — "honorific" is in the closed enum and is used for exactly this in batch-21 (gram:o-kudasai-2). Additionally, "request" is drawn from a single aside in the formation field ("Para pedidos, a negativa 〜てくれない？ é comum"), whereas the record's explanation and nuance fields are entirely about direction of benefit and gratitude ("a ação chega até você como um gesto bondoso", contrast with 〜てあげる/〜てもらう). The one tag carried is the record's secondary sense, not its primary one.

Variant 2 (negative) is [{base:verb, op:to-nai-stem},{op:append, token:"ないつもりでした"}]. Executed literally, to-nai-stem yields the nai-form minus い (書か-な / 食べ-な / し-な / こ-な), which is the semantics the task spec fixes with its own worked example (なければいけない = to-nai-stem + append "ければいけない" ⇒ 書かな+ければいけない) and the semantics 51 variants across batches 02-33 use (+"い"→書かない, +"かったら"→行かなかったら, +"くてもいい"→書かなくてもいい, +"いで"→待たないで). Appending a token that itself begins with ない therefore doubles the negative. The direct sibling record batch-10 gram:tsumori encodes the identical shape correctly as to-nai-stem + "いつもりです" → 書かないつもりです. The variant's own `example` field (書かないつもりでした) is right, which is exactly what hides the defect: the example does not follow from the steps. Fix: token "いつもりでした".

problems.issue: Variant 2 is [{base:verb, op:to-nai-stem},{op:append, token:"ないうちに"}]. Same defect as gram:n3-tsumori-deshita: to-nai-stem already produces 降ら-な / 書か-な / 食べ-な / し-な / こ-な per the spec's なければいけない example and the 51 sibling variants, so a token starting with ない doubles the negative. Compare batch-28 gram:n3-nai-to, which encodes the same 〜ない+particle shape as to-nai-stem + "いと" → 書かないと. The stated example 降らないうちに is correct but is not what the steps generate. Variants 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of this record all execute correctly (話しているうちに, 降っていないうちに, 高いうちに, 静かなうちに, 学生のうちに) and match the record's formation field. Fix: token "いうちに".

problems.issue: The record's formation says the clause closes with だ (informal) or です (formal) as a free alternation over all four bases, but the variant list gives the です form only for verb and noun (variants 5 and 6). The i-adjective and na-adjective variants exist only in the だ form, so a consumer generating from these steps can build 高いというのだ and 学生だというのです but never 高いというのです or 静かだというのです. Nothing ungrammatical is produced — this is a coverage asymmetry, not a false rule. Either add the two missing polite variants or drop variants 5 and 6 and model だ/です as a single alternation.

nuance_tags contains "concession", which the record's own nuance field explicitly denies. That field reads: "Armadilha PT: não confunda com にしては ('para/considerando', que marca surpresa); にしても é concessivo ('mesmo que')" — i.e. the record states that にしても is the concessive one and にしては marks surprise against a standard. The batch nevertheless tags both points with "concession" (n3-ni-shitemo: ["concession"], n3-ni-shite-wa: ["concession","comparison"]), collapsing exactly the distinction the record warns about. Any consumer filtering by nuance_tags=concession pulls にしては into a concessive bucket and a drill generator would present it as "mesmo que". "comparison" alone already covers the expectation-vs-reality contrast the explanation describes; "concession" should be dropped. Not a formation defect — no wrong Japanese is produced — so severity is minor.

The na-adjective variant emits 静かにしては, which is the exact ambiguity the same author declared blocking one record earlier. In n3-ni-shitemo they wrote steps_unavailable because 静かにしても "parses as the て-form of 静かにする plus も ... rather than the concessive this record teaches, so a generator would emit a well-formed sentence carrying the wrong construction." 静かにしては has the identical double parse (静かにする + ては = 'if you make it quiet'), yet it is encoded here. The stated reason for the split is that this record says 'sem な' while the sibling is silent, but that only settles whether な is kept — it does not remove the collision with 静かにする, which is what made the sibling unencodable. One of the two decisions is wrong and they should be reconciled. The output string is well-formed under at least one parse, so this is not critical; it is a generation hazard rather than an ungrammatical form.

nuance_tags includes "comparison", which the record does not support for THIS らしい. The explanation is purely indirect-source hearsay ("informação vem de algo que você ouviu, leu ou soube por uma fonte indireta, não de observação direta") — covered by hearsay + conjecture. The only comparison-flavoured content in the record is (a) a contrast drawn against ようだ/みたいだ, which is meta-commentary about a different grammar point, and (b) the record's explicit statement that there is "um らしい diferente que significa 'típico de'" (男らしい). Tagging comparison here imports the nuance of a pattern the record deliberately walls off, and looks derived from the label "parece que" rather than from the explanation. Formation steps are unaffected and correct.

nuance_tags is ["completion"], which is the tag that naturally denotes 〜たところだ / 〜たばかり ("acabar de fazer") — exactly the reading the record's own nuance warns against: "Cuidado para não confundir com outros usos de ところ: ～ているところ (estar no meio de algo) e ～たところだ (acabar de fazer) têm sentidos diferentes." The pattern's actual nuance per the explanation is discovery/finding-out after a completed action ("ao fazer X, descobri/aconteceu Y", "constatou um fato inesperado"), for which the closed enum has no member; an empty nuance_tags would be safer than one that collapses this record into the neighbour it is explicitly distinguished from. Formation steps (to-ta-form + ところ) are correct for all four verb classes.

The na-adjective variant {base:"na-adjective", op:"append", token:"にしては"} applied to 静か produces 静かにしては, whose live parse is 静かに + して + は — the て-form of 静かにする plus は, 'as for making it quiet' — not the surprise/concession construction this record teaches. A generator would emit a well-formed sentence carrying the wrong construction. Three independent confirmations that this is a real defect and not a judgement call: (1) the SAME batch file flags the identical string for the sibling point gram:n3-ni-shitemo, whose steps_unavailable reads 'Dropping it yields 静かにしても, a string that parses as the て-form of 静かにする plus も ... so a generator would emit a well-formed sentence carrying the wrong construction' — the author reasoned it through, then encoded the は twin anyway on the strength of the record's wording; (2) this corpus already encodes 静かにする as to-adverbial > append(する) at batch-16 gram:gp-80, so the colliding parse is live in the same data; (3) it is the only na-adjective attachment of this shape among all 495 points — every sibling connective keeps な, including わりには, which THIS record's own nuance field names as にしては's near-synonym (batch-33 gram:n3-wari-ni-wa => 静かなわりには; also 暇なくせに, 静かなせいで, and 静かなおかげで in this very batch). The record's formation field ('adjetivo-な (sem な) + にしては', corpus/grammar/n3.json id 441) is itself defective — な-adjectives are not listed as an attachment for にしては in standard references. Per failure mode F3, that upstream error was laundered into machine steps rather than flagged; the correct output was the same steps_unavailable the author used one point later, or dropping the na-adjective variant. Verb, i-adjective and noun variants of this point are correct (書くにしては, 書いたにしては, 安いにしては, 初心者にしては).

The single variant claims base "verb" (unrestricted) with to-masu-stem + たて, but the record's own nuance explicitly states the pattern is limited to a handful of established production verbs and that 食べたて is NOT said ("Limita-se a poucos verbos consagrados de ações com resultado físico e perceptível; não se diz 食べたて, por exemplo"). Executed literally: 焼く→焼きたて OK, 洗う→洗いたて OK, but 食べる→食べたて (the record's own counterexample), する→したて, くる→きたて are not Japanese. The morphology is right and the base enum has no way to say "verb, lexically restricted", so this is a scope/annotation gap rather than a wrong rule — but as it stands a consumer generating drills from these steps will emit the exact form the record warns against. Fix by recording the restriction (e.g. the same steps plus an explicit lexical-scope note, or steps_unavailable citing the closed verb set); do not simply drop the steps, since the 焼き/作り/洗い cases are correct.
problems.bad_output: 食べたて / したて / きたて

problems.issue: The second variant claims base "noun" with steps [{base:noun,op:none},{op:append,token:"しかない"}]. Executed against the mandated noun test case 学生, it emits 学生しかない. The ない in this pattern is the negative of the existential ある, so with an animate noun the required form is 学生しかいない — the steps produce the wrong existential verb. The record's own formation prose ("substantivo + しかない (só há X). Com substantivos contáveis e quantidades é onde aparece o sentido de 'só tem/restam'") explicitly scopes the noun use to countable nouns, and 学生 is countable, so the record does not narrow the base away from the failing class either. Only the record's own example 千円しかない (inanimate) was tested by the author. Fix: either narrow the noun variant to inanimate/quantity nouns, or split into two variants — inanimate → append しかない, animate → append しかいない. The verb variant (書くしかない / 食べるしかない / するしかない / 来るしかない) is correct and unaffected.

nuance_tags includes "comparison", which the record's explanation does not support. This record's explanation is exclusively about indirect information ("a informação vem de algo que você ouviu, leu ou soube por uma fonte indireta"), which "hearsay" and "conjecture" already cover correctly. The only comparison-flavoured material in the record is (a) the nuance paragraph contrasting らしい with ようだ/みたいだ/そうだ, which is a didactic contrast between grammar points rather than a nuance the pattern expresses, and (b) the "típico de / 男らしい" sense, which the record itself labels "um らしい diferente" — a distinct grammar point. Tagging comparison here pulls a different point's semantics into this record's mechanical index, so a consumer querying comparison patterns gets hearsay-らしい back. Drop "comparison"; the steps themselves are all correct.

Only the verb-た+きり variant is emitted. The record's own `formation` explicitly documents a second attachment the steps do not cover — "Também aparece com substantivo + きり no sentido de 'apenas/só' (ex.: 二人きり)" — and the `label` itself carries that sense ("desde que (e nunca mais) / só (きり)"). A noun variant [{base:'noun', op:'append', token:'きり'}] is derivable straight from the record (学生きり / 二人きり). As shipped, a generator consuming these steps cannot produce the 'só' half of the point the label advertises. Not a false rule — a coverage gap — but it is a gap the record itself supplies the material to close.

The i-adjective variant's steps are correct (to-attributive + ほど is grammatical), but the chosen example 高いほど illustrates the PROPORTIONAL ほど, which this record explicitly excludes and which lives in its own corpus record. n3-hodo's nuance says: "não confunda este ほど comparativo com o ほど proporcional de ば...ほど", and gram:n3-ba-hodo (structure_pattern ～ば～ほど) exists as a separate point. 高いほど standalone reads as 'the more expensive, the...' — the neighbouring point — not as this record's comparative ('não tão... quanto') or extent ('a ponto de') senses. An extent-sense example (痛いほど type) would demonstrate the record's own scope. The steps need no change; the example does.

The record's structure_pattern and its single `forms` entry are 必ずしも～とは限らない, but the four variants encode only the ～とは限らない tail; nothing carries the 必ずしも head that names the point. This is the same adverb-plus-tail shape that this very batch declared unrepresentable three times (どんなに～ことか, どんなに～ても, 決して～ない all got steps_unavailable with the reason 'the closed op enum has no prepend operation'), so the batch treats one structural class two different ways. Executing the steps is harmless in itself — 行くとは限らない, 高いとは限らない, 便利とは限らない, 学生とは限らない are all grammatical, and the record's own nuance says とは限らない can stand alone — but a consumer generating a production drill for this slug will emit the bare tail while labelling it 必ずしも～とは限らない, which the record calls the form that 'quase sempre aparece junto'. Either add a steps_unavailable-style note about the dropped adverb slot or apply the same verdict used for 決して～ない.

nuance_tags is ["conjecture"], which the record does not support. Its explanation defines っけ as memory retrieval — 'usada quando a pessoa tenta lembrar ou confirmar algo que sabia mas esqueceu no momento' — and the nuance field then explicitly rules out the neighbouring reading it could be confused with ('não é um simples "né?" de confirmação social (isso é ね); っけ carrega especificamente a ideia de "eu esqueci e estou tentando resgatar da memória"'). Conjecture is inference about an unknown proposition; っけ is recall of a known one, so the tag looks derived from the interrogative label rather than from the record. The closed enum has no recall/confirmation value, and nuance_tags accepts zero entries, so [] would be the honest encoding. As it stands, a query for conjecture points groups っけ with かなあ, はずだ and でしょう. The formation_steps themselves are correct — 書いたっけ, 高かったっけ, 静かだっけ, 学生だっけ, 書きましたっけ, 学生ですっけ all match the record's formation field.

Corpus-wide ambiguity in the `to-nai-stem` op boundary, provable at this exact slug. Batch-27 treats `to-nai-stem` as yielding the stem of the NAI-adjective (書かな / 食べな / しな / こな) and carries the final い inside the append token ("いまま"). Batch-19's `gram:mama` — the same grammar point at N4 — encodes the identical formation the other way: `to-nai-stem` + token "ないまま", i.e. the op yields 書か / 食べ. Both files claim the same op name with incompatible outputs, so under any single interpreter definition at most one executes correctly; the loser emits *食べいまま or *食べないないまま. Batch-27 is on the SPEC-CONFORMANT side — the authoring prompt's own worked example (なければいけない = to-nai-stem + "ければいけない") only produces 書かなければいけない if the stem is 書かな, and batch-27 matches that, as do batches 05, 08, 12, 13, 14, 15, 20, 23, 25, 26, 28, 31, 33. The divergent minority is batch-06 (gp-7, hou-ga-ii), batch-19 (koto-ga-aru, koto-ni-naru, koto-ni-suru, mama), batch-24 (you-ni-suru, you-ni-you-na) and batch-32 (n3-tsumori-deshita, n3-uchi-ni). Flagging so the fix is applied to those batches and NOT to batch-27, and so the op enum gets a written definition before any generator consumes it. Applied literally under batch-27's own definition, all four of this point's to-nai-stem outputs are grammatical (書かないまま, 食べないまま, しないまま, こないまま).

The single variant claims base "verb" with no restriction: to-masu-stem + たて. Executed literally on the required test bases it yields 書きたて, 食べたて, したて, きたて. The record's own nuance field explicitly rules the second one out: "Limita-se a poucos verbos consagrados de ações com resultado físico e perceptível; não se diz 食べたて, por exemplo." So the steps generate a form the record itself names as impossible — an F1/F5 over-generation (a general rule contradicted by the entry's own text). The morphology is correct; the defect is that ～たて is lexically restricted to a closed set of production verbs (the record names only 焼く/作る/洗う) and the steps assert full productivity over all verbs. Fix: either steps_unavailable citing the lexical restriction, or keep the steps and narrow the claim so a generator cannot apply them to arbitrary verbs.

nuance_tags is ["continuation"] only, which encodes just the progressive half of the record and omits the half the record spends its PT trap warning about. The explanation states both senses — "Marca uma ação em andamento (...) ou o estado resultante de uma ação já concluída" — and the nuance is entirely about the second: "～ている nem sempre é o nosso gerúndio. Com verbos como 知る, 結婚する, 死ぬ ele indica estado (知っている = sei, 結婚している = sou casado), não ação em curso." The closed enum carries "completion", which is the tag for the resultative-state reading. As tagged, a consumer filtering by nuance sees ている as purely durative, i.e. exactly the misreading the record exists to correct. Steps themselves (ている / ていた / てる, incl. the で-voicing via to-te-form) all execute correctly.

Partial encoding of a two-slot correlative, reported as complete. The record's structure_pattern is ～ばかりか～も and its formation ends 'o segundo membro recebe a partícula も. Padrão: A ばかりか B も.' The five variants encode only the A-half (書くばかりか / 高いばかりか / 静かであるばかりか / 学生ばかりか / 学生であるばかりか — all grammatical when executed against 書く・食べる・する・くる・高い・静か・学生), and steps_unavailable is left "", which signals full coverage of a point whose identity is the pairing (label: 'não só... como também (ばかりか... も)'). This diverges from how the corpus handles the structurally identical 'not only A but also B' frame: batch-33 gram:n3-wa-mochiron-mo (～はもちろん～も) is declared steps_unavailable as 'Two-slot frame, not a single derivation', and batch-29 gram:n3-no emits a partial variant WITH a steps_unavailable note ('Encoded as far as a suffixing rule reaches'). Fix is either of those two treatments — do not add the second slot as an append token. Note this is coverage/labelling only: nothing here licenses a wrong form, and the な-adjective slot was correctly restricted to である (bare 静かばかりか would have been ungrammatical, and the record's ambiguous 'na+adjetivo ... podem levar である' could have invited it).

The steps encode the clause-FINAL attachment (Clause A + ですから), which is what the record's `formation` field describes and matches its example 寒いですから exactly - but they do not match the record's `structure_pattern` and `forms`, both of which are "ですから～" with the tilde AFTER, i.e. the sentence-initial connective ("portanto/então", which the pt-BR label also glosses). All four variants produce grammatical Japanese (書きますから, 寒いですから, 静かですから, 学生ですから), so nothing wrong is licensed; the defect is that the record is internally ambiguous (structure_pattern/forms say initial, formation says final) and the output silently picked one reading without flagging the other as unrepresented. A consumer generating a drill from these steps would target 書きますから for a point whose stored `form` is "ですから～". Either add a steps_unavailable-style note that the sentence-initial ですから sense cannot be encoded (no prepend op), or the record needs an upstream fix.

The record's formation says "Adjetivos e substantivos aparecem com なら + よかった" (adjectives, plural — both types — and nouns). The batch emits variants for verb, na-adjective and noun, but no i-adjective variant at all: neither 高いならよかった (the なら route the record names) nor 高ければよかった (the ば route the pattern is named after). A consumer asked to build ばよかった on 高い has nothing to apply. Nothing ungrammatical is generated — this is under-coverage, not a false rule — but the steps do not match what the record's own formation field states.

Base coverage does not match the record's own formation field. The record licenses FOUR attachments — 'Anexa-se a substantivos (substantivo + なんか) e tambem a verbos e adjetivos na forma simples (informal): verbo-simples + なんか, adjetivo-い + なんか, adjetivo-な + なんか', with its own example ピアノなんかも弾ける — but the output emits only the noun variant and leaves steps_unavailable as the empty string, so nothing records that the three documented attachments were dropped on purpose. Sibling batches emit one variant per documented base for the same kind of particle (gram:n3-kurai -> noun/verb/i-adjective; gram:n3-bakari -> noun + verb-te). Nothing ungrammatical is generated, so this is a coverage/traceability gap, not an F5: either add the verb (to-dictionary + なんか -> 書くなんか), i-adjective (高いなんか) and na-adjective (静かなんか) variants, or keep noun-only and say in steps_unavailable why the record's plain-form attachments were judged too shaky to emit.

The five variants encode only the first member of a two-member pattern and give no signal that they do. structure_pattern is ～ばかりか～も and the record's formation ends 'o segundo membro recebe a particula も. Padrao: A ばかりか B も', but the steps stop at 書くばかりか / 静かであるばかりか and steps_unavailable is empty, so a consumer reading the record programmatically cannot tell the も member exists. Precedent runs both ways and either is acceptable: gram:n3-wa-mochiron-mo (～はもちろん～も, structurally identical: suffix on member A, も on member B) was given steps_unavailable as a two-slot frame, while gram:n3-no emitted its one expressible variant AND a steps_unavailable note ('Encoded as far as a suffixing rule reaches'). The defect here is the empty note, not the variants — every emitted form is grammatical.
